text: The comparator is "medical rate- or rhythm-control therapy." RAFT-AF permitted rate control using medical therapy and/or atrioventricular-junction ablation with pacemaker treatment, so the included comparator was not exclusively medical therapy.

The question applies generally to "adults with atrial fibrillation and heart failure." The two contributing populations were materially narrower: CASTLE-AF involved heart failure with an implanted defibrillator, while RAFT-AF involved heart failure with high-burden atrial fibrillation. These restrictions are not carried into the headline population.

Eligibility criteria are recorded with provenance and the page marks property P3_inclusion_criteria as HELD. No population, intervention, comparator or study-design eligibility criteria are displayed. The dedicated table contains only em dashes, and the preconditions section separately says there is "no key screening.eligibility." A reader therefore cannot reproduce inclusion decisions.

"The PRISMA 2020 flow counts are held for this review and reconcile with the executed searches above" and "The unscreened remainder is 0." The page also states that no screening log exists and displays empty screening and per-trial disposition tables. The asserted screening counts and zero remainder cannot be audited from the reader-facing evidence.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." Although the two hazard ratios, confidence intervals, analysed denominators and event counts are displayed, the canonical object is absent, the Sources table is empty, and the screening and eligibility records needed to rebuild the inventory are not displayed.

"Estimand | time-to-first-event — random-effects" No random-effects model or any other pooled model was fitted. Random-effects is a synthesis model, not part of the estimand, and the page elsewhere explicitly says there was "NO model call."
"What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm." The page gives arm-level event counts for both trials: 51 versus 82 for CASTLE-AF and 50 versus 64 for RAFT-AF.

"Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: deviations from the intended intervention on 2 result(s), selection of the reported result on 2 result(s)." The page says no final risk-of-bias judgement exists, and its displayed D2 deviations judgements are "no information" for both assessors and both trials. The asserted two deviations-based ratings do not match the page's own table.

"Figure 1 not drawn ... A forest plot is the pooled claim in picture form." The Analysis Suite visibly displays a forest plot of the two unpooled trial estimates and offers SVG and PNG downloads. The paper section therefore contradicts another reader-facing part of the same page.

The screening cascade repeatedly classifies records by "the topic drug's role in the trial." This topic concerns an ablation procedure, not a drug. The drug-role terminology is stale boilerplate and does not coherently describe the intervention classification performed on this page.

The page discusses CABANA in explaining the phase-filter boundary. CABANA is named without its registration identifier where its identity is invoked; the supplied candidate record identifies it as NCT00578617.

The extraction method twice invokes the "96 per cent EAST-AFNET 4" interval. EAST-AFNET 4 is named without a registration identifier anywhere on the complete page, even though it is being used to explain a trial-specific confidence-interval calculation.

The review asks about catheter ablation versus medical rate- or rhythm-control therapy on death, stroke and hospitalisation. The displayed analysis instead evaluates each trial's different primary composite. CASTLE-AF omits stroke, CABANA includes serious bleeding and cardiac arrest but not hospitalisation, and RAFT-AF includes outpatient heart-failure treatment. The analysis therefore does not answer the stated outcome question.

Four sham-controlled trials are described as “the cleanest available form of this review's question”. A sham procedure is not the stated comparator of medical rate- or rhythm-control therapy. These trials may answer an efficacy-versus-sham question, but they do not directly instantiate the page's stated comparison.

“Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page.” The three displayed hazard-ratio rows are numerically rebuildable, but the review inventory and screening numbers are not. The canonical-object location is an em dash, the Sources table is empty, the eligibility-criteria table contains only em dashes, and the screening tables contain no trial-level dispositions.

The “What was measured” table names the estimand as “time-to-first-event — random-effects”. Random-effects is a synthesis model, not an estimand, and the page repeatedly states that no model was fitted because nothing was pooled.

The paper section states that Figure 1 was not drawn because “A forest plot is the pooled claim in picture form”. The Analysis Suite visibly displays two forest plots of the three trial estimates, so the page simultaneously says the forest plot was not drawn and shows it twice.

The risk-of-bias figure presents the included trials and says every cell carries both assessments. The figure renders CASTLE-AF, CABANA and RAFT-AF and then renders their three corresponding NCT identifiers as additional all-not-assessed rows. This duplicates the same three trial identities and can be read as six trials.
“The agreement rate is withheld pending adjudication.” The page later publishes the agreement rate as 40.0%, despite saying it is withheld and not interpretable.

The limitations state that the review does not give “the number of events in each arm”. Arm-level event counts are displayed for CASTLE-AF and RAFT-AF, although they are absent for CABANA. The accurate limitation is that event counts are incomplete, not wholly absent.

The stated scope includes “ablation against medical therapy” in atrial fibrillation. At least two completed trials not named by the page fit that population, intervention and comparator: CRAFT studied cryoablation versus antiarrhythmic drugs in persistent atrial fibrillation, and the CABANA pilot studied ablation versus drug therapy for atrial fibrillation. No displayed eligibility criterion explains their exclusion.

“Scope | one randomised trial (cabana) and eight matched population studies, ablation against medical therapy” The page actually presents four randomised trials—CASTLE-AF, CABANA, EAST-AFNET 4 and RAFT-AF—and displays no set of eight matched-population studies.

The page describes its subject as ablation and elsewhere as “ablation against medical therapy.” EAST-AFNET 4 did not randomise participants to ablation versus medical therapy; it compared an early rhythm-control strategy, which could use antiarrhythmic drugs or ablation, against usual care. The page itself acknowledges that this trial does not make the stated ablation comparison.

The administrative table labels “In Ablation and rhythm control in atrial fibrillation, what do the contributing trials show?” as the “Review question (PICO).” This is not a rebuildable PICO: it specifies no clinical population, operational intervention, comparator or common outcome, and the page states that eligibility criteria were not recorded.

The extracted-value table, contributing-trial table and forest plots label all four effects as odds ratios, including “CASTLE-AF primary | OR 0.62” and “OR (log scale).” All four displayed source analyses are hazard ratios from time-to-event analyses, not odds ratios. The page later correctly says that every row now carries the trial's reported hazard ratio, directly contradicting the reader-facing labels.

The “What was measured” table states “Estimand | not recorded ... — random-effects.” No random-effects model or estimator was fitted because no outcome was pooled; “random-effects” is a stale statistical-method label.

“This review reports against PRISMA 2020. A screening record is held on this object and the flow it supports is shown in the Methods.” The same page says no screening log was recoverable, reports no records-identified or exclusion counts, and shows no PRISMA flow.

The Paper section says “Figure 1 not drawn” because “A forest plot is the pooled claim in picture form.” The Analysis section visibly presents two forest plots of the four trial estimates. They omit a pooled estimate, but the assertion that a forest plot was not drawn contradicts the delivered page.

The Limitations section says: “What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm.” The page displays arm-level event counts for every trial: CASTLE-AF 51 versus 82, CABANA 89 versus 101, EAST-AFNET 4 249 versus 316, and RAFT-AF 50 versus 64.

EAST-AFNET 4 is described as “a strategy arm in which most patients received antiarrhythmic drugs.” The displayed registry evidence identifies early standardised rhythm control but provides no treatment-distribution numbers establishing that most participants received antiarrhythmic drugs.

The page presents four included trials as its evidence inventory: "It examines 4 randomised trials." The page cannot establish that these are all eligible trials because it states that no bibliographic search was run, provides no eligibility criteria, and has no screening record.

The administrative table labels the question "Review question (PICO)". The stated question contains no defined population, intervention or comparator; it merely asks what the contributing trials show for several outcome names. The page separately confirms that the comparator and eligibility criteria are not recorded.

"In the three trial-declared outcomes named in the title, what do the contributing trials show?" Four distinct registered primary-outcome formulations are displayed. The title omits ISAR-REACT 5's registered primary, "Composite of death, myocardial infarction or stroke," even though that trial is analyzed.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page" and "each measured cell names the source analysis it was read from." The canonical object is unavailable, arm-level event counts are absent, all four source-sentence fields say no source sentence was recorded, and every per-trial source cell is only ":". The displayed odds ratios therefore cannot be independently rebuilt from the page.

"A screening record is held on this object and the flow it supports is shown in the Methods." Elsewhere the page says no screening record was recoverable and no identified or excluded-record counts exist. No flow is displayed in the supplied page.

"No pooled estimate was produced for this outcome, so no model was fitted and none is described." The page nevertheless names "random-effects," reports a withdrawn pooled odds ratio, and reports I-squared and Cochran Q. These are remnants of a fitted synthesis and contradict the claim that no model or synthesis was applied.

For ISAR-REACT 5, the page says "death is unqualified and therefore all-cause." The registry wording shown on the page says only "death," and the page expressly reports that the registry provides no description. Unqualified wording does not by itself establish the adjudicated death definition.

The trial-characteristics table describes PLATO as "Clopidogrel (treatment, n=9333) vs Ticagrelor (control, n=9291)" and TWILIGHT as "Aspirin + Ticagrelor (treatment, n=3555) vs Placebo + Ticagrelor (control, n=3564)." Both arm descriptions are inverted. The page's own qualification says PLATO's 9333 participants received ticagrelor and its 9291 received clopidogrel, while TWILIGHT's 3555 received placebo plus ticagrelor and its 3564 received aspirin plus ticagrelor.

"Figure 1 not drawn" because "A forest plot is the pooled claim in picture form." The Analysis section visibly supplies two forest-plot renderings of the four individual estimates. A forest plot can display unpooled estimates, so its presence also does not imply a pooled claim.

The references map "ASPIRE / MTN-020" to NCT01539226 and "The Ring Study" to NCT01617096. The trial identities are reversed: the registry identifies NCT01617096 as ASPIRE, so assigning ASPIRE to NCT01539226 and The Ring Study to NCT01617096 is false.

The risk-of-bias and overall-judgement tables identify the contributing trials as "Aspire / MTN-020" and "The Ring Study". Those rows omit the NCT identifiers where trial identity is required. "The Ring Study" is only a descriptor, and the separate reference mapping that might resolve it is itself reversed.

The page repeatedly states, "This review is named for adolescent girls and young women," and applies an indirectness downgrade on that basis. The displayed title and PICO specify women, not adolescent girls and young women. Both registered trials enrolled women within that stated adult-inclusive scope, so an age mismatch with an undisclosed AGYW scope cannot honestly be presented as a mismatch with the page's stated question.

"Neither trial enrolled an adolescent" and "No participant under 18 was eligible for either trial." The second statement does not establish the first. Eligibility of ages 18–45 does not provide participant-level minimum ages, and the page never defines adolescence as ending before age 18; therefore the categorical enrollment claim goes beyond the displayed evidence.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The page supplies per-trial risk ratios and confidence intervals but omits arm-level events and denominators. The contributing-trials table has no trial rows, the visual abstract reports "n/a participants," and the trial-characteristics table says randomised counts were not extracted. A reader cannot rebuild the trial effects or audit the pooled result from the displayed inputs.

"The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article." No Extended data or verbatim model call/output appears anywhere in the complete page supplied to the reader.

The visual abstract says "GRADE certainty: not rated," while the Summary of findings and manuscript report Low certainty. The page gives incompatible certainty statuses for the same outcome. It also says the downgrade domains are not recorded, then displays detailed risk-of-bias and indirectness rating steps.

"No risk-of-bias assessment is recorded." The page contains a RoB-2 table, overall judgements for both trials, and a manuscript section stating that risk of bias was assessed independently by two assessors. The quoted limitation is stale and contradicts the page's own evidence.

"The agreement rate is withheld pending adjudication" and a rate across 10 domain comparisons "is not reported." The risk-of-bias figure later reports the same domain agreement explicitly as 8 of 10, or 80%.

The administrative table states: “Two independent screeners of different model families, title/abstract then full text, with named human adjudication.” No second independent screen was performed; the paper later explicitly refuses that claim.
The synthesis methods were “all pre-specified before the search.” The page says there was no prespecified protocol and that eligibility criteria were derived post hoc.

The page says the PRISMA counts are recorded and reconcile, the unscreened remainder is zero, and “Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page” is available. The same page says no screening log exists; its inclusion-criteria, remainder-screening and every-trial disposition tables are empty. A reader cannot reconstruct how 99 surfaced records became eight included trials.

The pooled result has eight trials, and the extraction section promises “One row per extracted value.” The extraction, contributing-trials and endpoint-definition tables contain only six trials. NCT02289963 and NCT02585778 appear in the forest plot and model input but lack the displayed extraction/provenance and analysed denominators supplied for the other trials.

The visual abstract reports “8 trials, n/a participants.” Participant denominators are not fully reported even though the page presents analysed treatment/control denominators for six trials and names registry records for all eight; the two added trials have no analysed denominators, and the trial-characteristics table says “not extracted” for every trial.

The page calls its registry verification complete: “SIX OF SIX CONTRIBUTING VALUES ARE THEREFORE CONFIRMED AGAINST THEIR REGISTRY RECORDS — the only topic in this lane where the trial-by-trial check is complete.” The pooled analysis contains eight trials. The displayed comparison checks only six and omits NCT02289963 and NCT02585778, so the trial-by-trial check shown to the reader is not complete.

The visual abstract says its interval is “drawn CROSSING the no-difference line because it does.” The displayed 95% confidence interval is -60.6 to -48.8 and therefore does not cross the no-difference value of zero; the same visual abstract correctly says elsewhere that the interval excludes no difference.

The visual abstract says “GRADE certainty: not rated,” and the Summary of Findings table displays an em dash. The paper later reports a completed GRADE assessment of LOW certainty for the same eight-trial outcome.

The page alternately says risk of bias is “not computable” and that RoB 2 was applied with “6 result-level assessments”; it labels the displayed table as covering “every included result.” Only six of the eight contributing results have rows, NCT02289963 and NCT02585778 are absent, and the displayed reasons show only D1–D4 despite the text relying on D5. The risk-of-bias assessment is internally contradictory and incomplete.

The administrative table says: “Funnel, Egger and Peters, each reported as a computed value.” The page reports no funnel result and no computed Egger or Peters statistic; later language only says such methods have little power below ten studies.

The quoted statistical output calls the DerSimonian–Laird analysis “THE FIT THAT PRODUCED THE SERVED NUMBER.” The served headline is the REML result, -54.72 (-60.62 to -48.82); the DerSimonian–Laird result is an obsolete sensitivity estimate retained under a stale heading.

The page reports "2 registered trials" and identifies only two additional eligible but unreported trials. The stated scope also encompasses at least NCT00644943, a completed pediatric trial explicitly comparing amoxicillin/clavulanate with cefdinir. The page imposes no comparator restriction and even treats unreported registrations as eligible, so this trial cannot be omitted on either ground.

"Amoxicillin in young children with acute otitis media" The displayed trials concern amoxicillin-clavulanate rather than amoxicillin alone, and only one of the two included trials randomized that treatment. In NCT03818815, amoxicillin-clavulanate was background therapy in every arm while OP0201 was the randomized intervention. The page therefore does not consistently study the intervention named in its title and question.

The review question is presented as a "Review question (PICO)". It does not define a comparator or a specific clinical outcome; "a registered clinical endpoint" is an endpoint category rather than a prespecified outcome. Consequently, the purported PICO does not provide reproducible eligibility boundaries.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The Sources table and Contributing trials table contain no rows, the canonical object is represented by an em dash, and the page displays neither the registered outcomes nor the per-trial endpoint-classification decisions supporting its central 2-of-2 claim. A reader cannot rebuild that claim from the displayed inputs.

"All 2 of 2 seeded registrations register no clinical endpoint at any rank." Both named registrations display clinical primary outcomes. NCT00377260 registers time to symptom resolution and weighted-average AOM symptom scores; NCT03818815 registers efficacy assessed by otoscopy. The premise used to withdraw the estimate and discuss high selective-reporting risk is therefore false.

"What it establishes is that a synthesis on this page pooled a clinical quantity that none of these registrations pre-specified." Elsewhere the page says no synthesis method was applied, reports k = 0, and shows the result as not pooled. It displays no historical or current pooled quantity from which this methodological conclusion could be checked. This is stale or contradictory language describing an analysis the page says it did not perform.

"1 of 2 trial was confirmed" and "1 trial was given in every arm". These trial-level findings use anonymous descriptors instead of identifying which statement applies to NCT00377260 and which applies to NCT03818815. The identifiers appearing elsewhere do not resolve the identity at the point where the contrasting trial claims are made.

“What was found. 3 registered trials” within the question “Anidulafungin Candida: is a pooled estimate possible?” The inventory omits registry trials that plainly fit the stated broad population, intervention and active-comparator scope. At minimum, NCT00058682 studies anidulafungin versus fluconazole for candidemia, NCT00056368 studies anidulafungin versus a comparator for candidemia or invasive candidiasis, and NCT01176058 studies anidulafungin versus fluconazole for candidemia and/or invasive candidiasis. The page states no eligibility restriction that excludes them.

The page asks broadly, “Anidulafungin Candida: is a pooled estimate possible?” The work actually evaluates an acknowledged convenience sample of three trials, without a search or screening process, so it cannot answer the broad subject-level question stated in the title and PICO.

“Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page.” The page cannot be rebuilt from what is displayed: the Sources table is empty, the registered-outcome sections contain no data, the Contributing trials table has no trial rows, the canonical object is shown as an em dash, and the page says only registry IDs were extracted. No per-trial outcome values, denominators or effect estimates are provided.

“3 of 3 trials were confirmed: the drug is part of the randomised comparison.” The displayed evidence does not establish this assertion for every trial. In particular, the supplied NCT00761267 information identifies a prospective open-label pediatric study and lists anidulafungin and fluconazole, but the page displays no allocation, arm structure or evidence that these were randomized comparison arms.

“A pooled result becomes possible if these trials report a shared clinical outcome.” The page itself says the trials already share global response and all-cause mortality at some rank, while also arguing that population heterogeneity prevents a clinically meaningful pool. A shared outcome alone therefore would not resolve the page's stated objection.

“Neutropenia changes both the infection and the outcome, because the host response that clears candidaemia is the response neutropenia removes.” This clinical causal assertion is not supported by any displayed trial result, subgroup estimate or clinical source. The cited MECIR passage supports assessing clinical similarity before pooling, but does not establish this specific biological claim or quantify effect modification by neutropenia.

“NCT00761267's registered primary is adverse events, not an efficacy outcome; the other two register global response.” The two global-response trials are referred to only as “the other two” at the point where their outcomes are interpreted. The reader must infer that this means NCT00805740 and NCT00806351, despite identifiers being available elsewhere.

The page asks broadly: "In Anidulafungin in invasive fungal infection, what is the effect on each trial's own registered primary outcome?" and reports only two trials. At least three unlisted randomized comparator trials fall within that stated scope: NCT00056368 studied anidulafungin versus comparator in candidemia/invasive candidiasis; NCT00058682 studied anidulafungin versus fluconazole in candidemia; and NCT01176058 studied anidulafungin versus fluconazole in candidemia and/or invasive candidiasis. The page states no eligibility restriction that excludes these populations or comparators.

"Anidulafungin in invasive fungal infection" The stated population and intervention scope is broad, but the page actually examines a convenience sample of two small, terminated phase 3 trials comparing anidulafungin with caspofungin in Candida infection. It does not cover the wider invasive-fungal-infection population implied by the title or even all randomized anidulafungin trials in invasive candidiasis.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The Sources table has no rows, the Contributing trials table has no trial rows, the canonical-object field is an em dash, and no per-trial effect estimate, confidence interval, estimator or effect scale is displayed. Arm results appear only in narrative prose, so the claimed effect on each trial's primary outcome cannot be reproduced as a specified analysis.

"Extracted per trial on this object: registry id. Fields not listed here were not extracted." The page nevertheless presents primary-outcome definitions, arm denominators and response results as if they were structured trial inputs. Their absence from the displayed extraction and contributing-trial tables prevents verification of how the narrative values map to the analysis object.

"Two trials that differ in population and report the outcome in different units" A response percentage and a response count with its denominator are two representations of the same dichotomous scale, not intrinsically different outcome units. The displayed values can be expressed uniformly as proportions. Differences in endpoint definition or timing might still prevent pooling, but the page does not establish those differences from the displayed data.

"The comparator arms hold 13 and 3 participants. A three-participant arm cannot support an interval worth displaying whatever the population." Small arms produce imprecise estimates and potentially very wide intervals, but they do not make an effect estimate or interval intrinsically undisplayable and do not by themselves prohibit meta-analysis. The cited similarity principle does not establish a minimum arm size.

"Neutropenia is not a co-label, it changes both the infection and the outcome: the host response that clears candidaemia is the response neutropenia removes, so 'global response' does not mean the same thing in the two trials." The registry material establishes that one trial enrolled patients with neutropenia, but the page displays no endpoint definitions or comparative evidence demonstrating that neutropenia changes the meaning of the registered global-response outcome. The mechanistic assertion therefore goes beyond the displayed evidence.

"A risk-of-bias assessment grades trials contributing to a pooled result; this page publishes none." Risk of bias is assessed for individual study results and remains relevant when trials are summarized separately or no meta-analysis is performed. The absence of a pooled estimate does not make risk-of-bias assessment inapplicable to the two trial results the page discusses.

The page presents "three direct comparisons" and states that every eligible registration is reported. At least one additional completed, result-bearing trial falls squarely within the stated scope: NCT00422084 compared pyronaridine-artesunate with Coartem (artemether-lumefantrine) in Plasmodium falciparum malaria. It is absent from the page.

"Two further eligible registrations post no results; they are listed under eligible_but_not_contributing and are not excluded." The completed direct comparison NCT06300970—artesunate-amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for Plasmodium falciparum malaria—has no posted registry results and fits the page's stated scope, but it is not named or listed as eligible-but-not-contributing.

"Among trials comparing an artemisinin-based combination therapy with artemether-lumefantrine" The stated question contains no age, disease-severity, species, pregnancy, setting, or geographic restriction, while all three displayed trials are pediatric studies of uncomplicated malaria. The evidence shown therefore represents a substantially narrower population than the question claims.

"Two further eligible registrations post no results; they are listed under eligible_but_not_contributing" No eligible_but_not_contributing section, registration identifiers, or disposition rows appear anywhere on the delivered page. Readers therefore cannot reconstruct or audit the claimed eligible-trial inventory.

Each comparison specifies "Effect scale | pooled on the log scale". Every comparison contains exactly one study and is explicitly labelled "Single cohort — no synthesis"; no pooled model or pooled estimator was fitted. The word "pooled" is stale or incorrect analytical language.

The network narrative says, "One trial dosed at home rather than under observation". This descriptor refers to NCT04565184 but does not carry its registration identifier at that point in the narrative, even though the identifier appears elsewhere.

The page is titled "Apixaban after acute coronary syndrome," implying a clinical review of apixaban's effects after ACS. The page evaluates only the registered bleeding outcomes of two phase 2 trials and presents no estimate of apixaban's clinical effects after ACS. The page itself acknowledges that its title implies a different question.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The page supplies denominators but no per-arm event counts, effect estimates, intervals, source sentences or usable source-cell citations. Its canonical object is also displayed as an em dash, so neither the withdrawn calculation nor its inputs can be rebuilt.

"Every row carries the value, the verbatim sentence it was read from, a resolvable link to the source, and whether the number was read or derived." Both extraction rows explicitly lack an effect value and source sentence, while the Sources table contains no source rows.

The methods table labels the estimand "bleeding events during the treatment period — random-effects" and says the effect scale was "reported on the log scale." No effect estimate is displayed or held, and the page expressly says no synthesis method was applied and nothing was pooled. Random-effects is a model rather than an estimand, and no displayed result establishes a log-scale analysis.

"GOSH plot — not drawn at this k" and "Computable but uninformative at k = 2." A GOSH analysis is not rebuildably computable from this page because both trial effect estimates and their uncertainty are absent. Counting two named trials does not supply the numerical inputs for subset meta-analyses.

For APPRAISE-1, the page says the 315-versus-599 imbalance "is what pooling several placebo strata against one dose stratum looks like." The displayed registry definition says the primary outcome combines two apixaban low-dose groups and placebo across phases. It does not support the page's assertion that several placebo strata were pooled against one dose stratum, and the absent event-level source data prevent verification of what the 315 and 599 represent.

The site card said "bleeding and efficacy endpoints pooled." The page displays no pooled result, and the registered primary outcome for each named trial is bleeding without an efficacy component. The page itself states that the card's explanation was false.

“What was found. 4 registered trials.” At least two unnamed registry trials fall within scopes already represented among the four included trials: OCEANIC-AF compares asundexian with apixaban for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation, matching the included PACIFIC-AF contrast; AXADIA compares apixaban with a vitamin-K antagonist in atrial fibrillation with end-stage kidney disease, matching the included RENAL-AF population and contrast.

“Does apixaban reduce stroke and systemic embolism in atrial fibrillation?” This is not the operative question represented by the included set: two trials have bleeding primary outcomes, PACIFIC-AF uses apixaban as the comparator for another anticoagulant, and RENAL-AF is restricted to patients with end-stage renal disease on haemodialysis. No eligibility criteria define why these populations, interventions, comparators and outcomes constitute one review scope.

“Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page.” The page does not provide rebuildable trial inputs. All four rows in the contributing-trials table report “not stated” for the effect and interval; event counts are not displayed there, the extracted-values table says no effect value is held, the sources table is empty, and the canonical-object field is an em dash. PACIFIC-AF is represented by only 249 and 254 analysed participants without naming the selected arms, although its registry enrollment is 755.

“Aristotle and averroes both favour it on their own registered efficacy endpoints”; “the two point in opposite directions”; and “the pooled direction was always going to be set by the efficacy trials.” The displayed tables contain no effect estimate or interval for any trial and no event value for AVERROES, PACIFIC-AF or RENAL-AF. Consequently, the asserted trial directions and the direction of the withdrawn pool cannot be checked from the evidence displayed.

“Estimand | first event — random-effects”; “Effect scale | reported on the log scale”; and “GOSH plot — not drawn at this k | Computable but uninformative at k = 4.” No random-effects model, log-scale effects or GOSH analysis was fitted or made computable on the displayed page: it elsewhere states that no synthesis method was applied, every effect value is absent, and the four trials do not measure a common outcome. “Random-effects” is also a synthesis model, not an estimand.

“3 of 4 trials were confirmed: the drug is part of the randomised comparison. 1 could NOT be decided this way.” The trial whose identity or arm structure remained unverified is referred to only as “1”; the summary supplies neither its trial name nor its NCT identifier, so a reader cannot determine which registration failed this check.

The review question asks about symptomatic venous thromboembolism and bleeding. The page reports only one pooled thromboembolism composite. It provides no bleeding synthesis, even though the fifth included trial, NCT02366871, has major and clinically relevant non-major bleeding as registered primary outcomes.

The efficacy question concerns "symptomatic venous thromboembolism." The pooled endpoint is proximal DVT, non-fatal pulmonary embolism, or VTE-related death without a displayed symptomatic restriction. The endpoint-definition table provides no descriptions or analysis windows establishing that the proximal DVT events were symptomatic.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The page displays analysed denominators and trial-level risk ratios but not the arm-level event rates or event counts used to derive those ratios. It therefore permits reproduction of the meta-analysis from supplied log estimates and standard errors, but not independent reconstruction of the trial effects from clinical outcome data.

The Trial characteristics table labels 2481, 4394, 2394 and 4494 as the numbers "Randomised," and the visual abstract calls their sum "13,763 participants." Those are the analysed denominators shown in the contributing-trials table, not the registry enrollment totals. The supplied registry records report n=3608 for NCT00371683, n=5407 for NCT00423319, n=3221 for NCT00452530 and n=6758 for NCT00457002.
The visual abstract states "GRADE certainty: not rated." The page's Summary of findings and Certainty sections rate the outcome VERY_LOW after three downgrades.

The GRADE explanation says the trial risk ratios include "two intervals excluding the null in opposite directions." The only two displayed intervals excluding RR=1 are ADVANCE-3, 0.1922 to 0.8293, and ADVANCE-2, 0.2590 to 0.9715; both favour apixaban. No displayed interval excludes the null in the opposite direction.

"The trials' results were loosely consistent with one another." The displayed statistics indicate substantial and statistically detectable heterogeneity: I²=71.48%, Q(3)=9.3122, p=0.0254, with trial risk ratios ranging from 0.399 to 1.407. The page itself rates certainty down for inconsistency.

The imprecision assessment says the interval 0.4371 to 1.264 "spans a 55% reduction and a 23% increase." Those limits correspond to approximately a 56.3% reduction and a 26.4% increase. The 23% figure belongs to the superseded upper limit of 1.2309 and was not updated when the interval changed.

The Methods state: "Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2." No result-level or domain-level RoB 2 assessment was performed: the page reports zero assessments and elsewhere says risk of bias is not computable.

The quoted analysis command is "rma(yi = yi, sei = sei, method = \"REML\", test = \"knha\")", while the page reports RR 0.7433 with a 95% interval of 0.4371 to 1.264. The quoted output identifies 0.4371 to 1.2639 as the unadjusted interval and 0.3067 to 1.8013 as both the Hartung-Knapp result and the "HOUSE INTERVAL." The screening log presents the review's current decisions for each trial. It labels ADOPT, ADVANCE-3 and ADVANCE-1 "eligible poolable not included," and ADVANCE-2 "needs adjudication," although all four are subsequently presented as contributing trials in the pooled analysis.

The page reports a single coherent participant count for the four-trial pool. The visual abstract reports 13,763 participants, while the withholding section says the same four-trial pool settled at 13,570 participants.

The page includes structured supporting tables for inclusion criteria, screening, withholding decisions and every trial's reason. Tables 15, 16, 18, 19 and 20 are empty or contain em dashes despite their headings and despite related prose appearing elsewhere, leaving important audit surfaces unrendered.

The page provides coherent information-source reporting. The administrative table says "0 source layers" and the Sources table is empty, while the Methods claim searches of ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed and the extraction rows rely on registry-posted results.

The review question asks about recurrent venous thromboembolism "and on bleeding." The page presents only a recurrent-VTE synthesis and explicitly acknowledges that it provides no measure of harm, so the bleeding component of its stated question is unanswered.

The page says, "Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The three-trial pooled calculation is substantially rebuildable, but the wider review is not: the search-result tables contain no identifiers, the Sources table is empty, the canonical-object field is an em dash, and the page says the query yield identifiers are not carried.

The headline and cascade state that eight trials reported a recurrent-VTE outcome and that the noncontributing trials are each named. The page does not provide a populated table mapping the claimed eight trials to their registered recurrent-VTE outcomes; its relevant withholding-question tables are empty, so a reader cannot reconstruct which exact eight support the headline count.

The endpoint table promises to show what each contributing trial counted, including rank and analysis set/window. For all three pooled trials, the registered-outcome rank and analysis set/window are displayed as em dashes, and every description cell says no description was recorded. This prevents the table itself from establishing endpoint timing and rank, despite those details being asserted elsewhere.

The visible qualifications state that the pool used "Paule-Mandel between-study variance" and call it "the same as the pool itself." The synthesis sections and quoted model call identify REML, not Paule-Mandel. The Paule-Mandel language is stale and names an estimator that the displayed analysis did not fit.

The page-standard assessment says, "No quotable model output exists" and that the pool "was computed outside R." The same page reproduces an R/metafor call and extensive model output under "Analysis output — recurrent_vte (quoted verbatim)," while the Results section also claims the full output is reproduced verbatim.
The visual abstract reports "GRADE certainty: not rated." The Summary of Findings and Certainty sections rate the same pooled outcome as very low certainty.

The visual abstract prominently labels the result "no difference." The interval ranges from 0.344 to 1.75 and therefore permits substantial benefit and harm; the page's own GRADE explanation says the answer is "not established" rather than "no difference."

The review says no final risk-of-bias judgement exists and that neither assessor's judgement is the review's finding. The GRADE assessment nevertheless downgrades risk of bias on the categorical premise that all three results are "some concerns overall," without identifying an adjudicated review-level judgement.

The Limitations section says, "What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm." The extraction and contributing-trials tables display all three sets of arm-level events and denominators: 32/576 versus 46/579, 15/1345 versus 14/1355, and 0/38 versus 1/40.

The page says every trial is keyed to a verified registration identifier. The risk-of-bias tables and graphic use the descriptors "(Japanese acute DVT/PE study)" and "(apixaban versus rivaroxaban)" in place of identifiers. These refer to NCT01780987 and NCT03266783 respectively, but that identity is not carried in those rows.

“What was found. 2 registered trials.” The inventory is incomplete even under the page's broad, comparator-unrestricted scope. At minimum, three completed, result-bearing apixaban trials directly concerning VTE treatment fall inside it: acute DVT/PE in NCT00643201, cancer-associated VTE in NCT03045406, and acute pediatric VTE in NCT02464969.

“In Apixaban VTE, what is the effect on each trial's own registered primary outcome?” No population, clinical setting, comparator, or eligibility boundary is defined. The two selected trials concern different populations and questions—postoperative thromboprophylaxis in women with suspected pelvic malignancy and heavy menstrual bleeding during anticoagulant comparison—and the page acknowledges that the set is merely a convenience sample. It therefore does not implement the broad question its title states.

The page presents sections for each trial's registered primary outcome and a contributing-trials table. It displays no per-trial outcome values, analyzed denominators, event counts or continuous-summary inputs, and no trial-level effect estimates. The contributing-trials table has no data rows, so readers cannot calculate either trial's effect or answer the page's stated question.

“Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page.” The page supplies no canonical object, registration location, source-layer entry, search record, or numerical trial inputs. Its own reproducibility table shows dashes where the artifact and registration should be, so the rebuildability claim is false.

“A pooled result becomes possible if these trials report a shared clinical outcome.” A shared outcome alone would not make these trials validly poolable: the page itself says their populations and comparators also differ. Pooling would additionally require a coherent common estimand and clinically compatible contrasts.

ANSWER-HF is excluded because it fails on the measure. The same page includes ANSWER-HF as the fourth trial in the primary hazard-ratio pool. The stale exclusion remains both in the narrative and in the manuscript screening table.
The primary outcome was pooled from 3 trials. The forest plot, contributing-trials table, visual abstract and primary model all contain 4 trials.

The manuscript PRISMA table reports 7 studies contributing to the synthesis. There are 7 included reports but only 4 contributing studies. The page's graphical PRISMA flow distinguishes these correctly.

The review contains “4 trials contributing 9,734 randomised participants.” 9,734 is the sum of the displayed analysed denominators. The page's stated randomised totals sum to 9,779: 8,442 + 922 + 225 + 190.

The number needed to treat is 22.6 (16.3 to 37.2), derived from a pooled risk difference of -0.0442. The current k=4 risk-difference analysis displayed immediately above is -0.0231 (-0.0629 to 0.0167). Its reciprocal point estimate is approximately 43, and its interval crosses no effect, so it cannot yield the displayed finite NNT interval. The NNT is stale from another analysis.

The outcome's GRADE certainty is Low. The page has no coherent certainty status: its summary-of-findings table says Low, while the visual abstract and dedicated GRADE section say Pending and not rated.

The final analysis inventory says the prediction interval and funnel/Egger analysis were not estimable, no Bayesian posterior was stored, and no subgroup analysis was stored. Earlier sections display a prediction interval, an Egger test, a Bayesian posterior and a post-hoc aetiology subgroup analysis. The final inventory is stale k=3 boilerplate.
The GRADE indirectness explanation refers to “The Chagas aetiology of one trial”. Two included trials are restricted to Chagas heart failure: PARACHUTE-HF and ANSWER-HF.

“ACTIVITY-HF: could not be resolved to any trial.” The same page lists a resolvable ACTIVITY-HF publication as PMID 34591356. The readiness warning uses an unresolved descriptor where the page already has an identity.
The screening log names a trial only as “Li 2019”. No NCT number, PMID, DOI or other resolvable trial identifier is supplied for this named trial.

No risk-of-bias domain in any included trial was rated high. ANSWER-HF, one of the four included trials, was not assessed at all. The unqualified manuscript statement therefore extends beyond the displayed assessment.

The discrepancy in PARACHUTE-HF serious adverse events was resolved because the registry and publication used different observation windows. The manuscript later labels the same discrepancy unresolved and says neither value was adopted, leaving the status of the safety evidence contradictory.

“Full build. Every randomised trial located ... is held and pooled.” The page simultaneously says its eligible-trial count is only a lower bound and that Li 2019 could be a missing eligible trial. Completeness is therefore not established.

The field labelled "Review question (PICO)" states: "Both trials register hierarchical endpoints analysed by win ratio, and the two hierarchies are not the same hierarchy." This is a methodological observation, not a PICO question: it does not state the population, intervention, comparator or clinical outcome. The page later acknowledges that "nothing on this page estimates the question its title implies."

The page variously states that both trial identities and topic-versus-control contrasts were verified. Its summary says only one of the two intervention identities was confirmed and the other remains unverified. The claim that all two trials contribute a verified topic-versus-control contrast therefore conflicts with the page's own verification result.

The page says the executed search strings, datetimes, filters and hit counts are displayed and later marks the search property HELD. The displayed search has no execution datetime or hit count, Table 2 is empty, and the page expressly says the query yield is not held.

The extraction section says every row carries the extracted value, verbatim source sentence and resolvable source, while the reproducibility section says: "Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." Neither trial has a displayed effect estimate or source sentence. The contributing-trials table gives "not stated" intervals and a source cell containing only a colon, so a reader cannot rebuild or verify either trial result.

For ATTRibute-CM, the page displays analysed treatment/control counts of 409/202. Those counts total 611, whereas the supplied registry record reports enrolment of 632. The page supplies neither an analysis-population definition nor an explanation for the 21-participant difference.

The methods table describes the estimand as "hierarchical composite — random-effects" and says the effect scale was "reported on the log scale." No effect estimate is displayed, nothing was pooled and the page repeatedly says no statistical model was run. Random effects is a model specification, not an estimand, and the page supplies no result supporting a log-scale analysis.

The core claim is that both registered primary endpoints were "analysed by win ratio." The displayed registry descriptions name the Finkelstein-Schoenfeld method and report total or percentage wins, but no displayed source states a win-ratio estimate or supplies such an estimate and variance. The page therefore does not substantiate its named estimator from the evidence it displays.

The page says: "The agreement rate is withheld pending adjudication." The analysis section nevertheless publishes a per-domain agreement rate of 60.0% and an overall agreement tally, directly contradicting the withholding statement.

The summary says: "No pooled estimate, risk-of-bias assessment or certainty rating is published for this question." Tables 4 and 5 publish two assessors' domain-level and overall risk-of-bias assessments. They are unadjudicated and not final, but they are still displayed assessments, so the summary wording is stale or materially incomplete.

The extraction and risk-of-bias tables identify trials only as ATTR-ACT and ATTRibute-CM. The corresponding registrations are NCT01994889 and NCT03860935, but Tables 3 through 5 omit those identifiers where the trial-specific values and judgements are presented. Identifiers appearing in later tables do not make these trial-result rows independently resolvable.

The page labels its question as a PICO: "In Patisiran, vutrisiran and eplontersen in hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloid polyneuropathy, what do the contributing trials show?" This is not an operational PICO: eligibility criteria, comparator, study design, outcome-selection rule and eligible trial status are unspecified. Consequently, the page's intended trial universe cannot be determined.

"It pools 3 randomised trials." Only APOLLO supplies a randomized concurrent placebo contrast. HELIOS-A uses APOLLO's external placebo cohort, and NEURO-TTRansform uses the external placebo cohort from NCT01737398; therefore the three displayed effects are not three randomized concurrent-control contrasts.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The page does not display the per-arm sample sizes, means, changes, standard deviations or standard errors needed to reconstruct the three mean differences. The contributing-trials table also reports both intervention and control as "not stated," the source cells as ":", and the canonical object as an em dash.

"The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article." No Extended data section or model call, estimator output or heterogeneity statistics appears anywhere in the complete page supplied to the reader.

The page states both "The pooled estimate for this outcome has been WITHDRAWN" and "This pool is referred, not withdrawn... The estimate is unchanged." The status of the same analysis is internally contradictory: elsewhere the summary says "not pooled," while the page continues to display the three effects and a previously pooled estimate. A clinician cannot determine whether the synthesis was withdrawn, merely referred, or still operative.

"It reports that both 'consistently demonstrated significant improvements' in neuropathy, quality of life and cardiac function, narratively." The displayed evidence contains only three mNIS+7 mean differences. It displays no quality-of-life or cardiac-function results capable of supporting this clinical statement.

"A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without" event counts, absolute effects or numbers needed to treat. The displayed effect measure is a continuous-outcome mean difference on the natural mNIS+7 scale, not a relative effect or event-based risk measure. This limitation is stale boilerplate and misdescribes the evidence actually shown.

In the pooled-result explanation, the external-control trial is identified only as "NEURO-TTR": "the borrowed group is NEURO-TTR's." The descriptor stands in for NCT01737398 at that occurrence. Although the identifier appears later on the page, the trial is not resolvably identified where it first supplies a crucial external comparator.

"This review reports against PRISMA 2020. A screening record is held on this object and the flow it supports is shown in the Methods." The same page says no screening record was recoverable, gives no identification or exclusion counts, and displays no PRISMA flow.

"Figure 1 not drawn. this pool was withdrawn" and "A forest plot is the pooled claim in picture form, so drawing one here would restate the very combination this review retracted." The Analysis Suite nevertheless displays a forest plot of all three effects and supplies SVG, PNG, EPS and TIFF versions. The manuscript's figure statement does not match the page readers receive.

The title describes "the two trials that share both arms." Four trials share the specified intervention and comparator arms: NCT00846365, NCT00996281, NCT01033071 and NCT01309828. Only two are poolable for the selected blood-pressure outcome.

The pooled trials had an already shared estimand and "Nothing had to be harmonised." NCT00846365 measures the primary outcome at week 8, whereas NCT01033071 measures it at week 12. Time point is part of the estimand, so these are not identical quantities.

The reproducibility section says: "Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The displayed material does not identify the analyzed dose arm, whether the two azilsartan/chlorthalidone arms were combined, or the treatment and control denominators. It therefore cannot establish the contrast or shared-control handling behind either trial-level effect.

The extraction section says every row carries a verbatim source sentence and states whether the number was read or derived. Neither effect row has a source sentence, and both say it is not stated whether the value was read or derived.

The page says a random-effects model was fitted using REML and reports tau-squared, I-squared and Q. Its analysis-output panel instead says no model was run and that heterogeneity is undefined. These statements cannot both describe the displayed synthesis.

The visual-abstract commentary says the interval is drawn crossing the no-difference line "because it does." The visual abstract displays MD -5.69 with 95% CI -7.3 to -4.08 and explicitly says that this interval excludes no difference.

Table 6 reports n=2156 for the synthesis. The visual abstract reports "n/a participants," trial characteristics say randomized counts were not extracted, and no arm-level comparison denominators are shown. The displayed participant count is therefore internally unresolved and cannot be interpreted as the analyzed comparison sample.

The page includes a table titled "Named on this review, contributing nothing to its pool." The two non-poolable trials are rendered as anonymous question-mark rows, and narrative references identify them only as the two long-term safety studies with n=837 and n=153. These correspond to NCT00996281 and NCT01309828.
The visual abstract says "GRADE certainty: not rated." The Summary of Findings and manuscript both report Low certainty.
The Methods state: "Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2." No result-level risk-of-bias assessment was performed for either contributing result.

The limitations say the review lacks "any absolute effect or number needed to treat" and that "A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient." The analyzed outcome is continuous and the displayed mean difference in mmHg is already an absolute effect on that scale; event counts and number needed to treat are not the natural reconstruction inputs for this outcome. This is stale binary-outcome boilerplate.

The page asks for the effect of bamlanivimab versus placebo on each trial's registered primary outcome. The only named registration, BLAZE-1, contains several interventions and four registered primary outcomes, but the page never identifies the particular arm comparison or primary outcome answering its stated question.

"A single trial is reported as a single trial" and the page asks "what is the effect on each trial's own registered primary outcome?" No single-trial effect is displayed. The contributing-trials table has no trial row, endpoint, treatment/control values, denominators, event counts, interval, or effect estimate.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The page withholds the canonical object, registration location, search record, screening record, endpoint definitions, and numerical trial inputs, so its results cannot be independently rebuilt.

"No pooled estimate, risk-of-bias assessment or certainty rating is published for this question, because there is no combined result for them to describe." The absence of pooling does not remove the need to assess risk of bias in the single trial or certainty in the resulting single-study evidence. Those assessments are missing from a page framed for clinical interpretation.

"Each is registered and reports its own primary." The displayed page does not present any registered endpoint definition or result for NCT04427501, so a reader cannot verify this reassurance or determine what the trial found.

"A pooled result becomes possible when a second eligible trial reporting the same outcome is published." A second trial alone does not establish a valid pool: its estimand, intervention, comparator, outcome definition, time point, and effect scale must also be sufficiently compatible.

The page repeatedly says that it includes four registrations: "One trial answers this; the other three registrations on this page measure something else." The current page reports 21 surfaced registrations, screens 16 remainder trials, and records only one included trial. The four-registration description is stale and contradicts the displayed inventory.

"Every row carries the value, the verbatim sentence it was read from, a resolvable link to the source, and whether the number was read or derived." The sole extraction row has no source sentence, and its provenance field contradictorily labels the estimate both derived and read.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The displayed reproducibility artifact does not identify or link the canonical object or registration, the Sources table is empty, and the page elsewhere reports zero source layers.

The synthesis-method field says "Pooled under single study-effects" and the forest plots label the result "Pooled (HR)." No synthesis model or pooled estimator was fitted; the displayed HR is NCT02993406's own registered single-trial estimate.

The visual abstract says "GRADE certainty: not rated," and the Summary says "No ... certainty rating is published for this question." The Summary of findings assigns Low certainty and says it was downgraded for risk of bias and imprecision. The page therefore gives mutually incompatible certainty messages.

The page assigns Low certainty because of risk of bias while also stating that no final risk-of-bias judgement exists. The displayed basis for the certainty downgrade is internally incoherent: assessor judgements remain unadjudicated and the page expressly disclaims a final risk-of-bias finding.

"The agreement rate is withheld pending adjudication. It is not reported." The analysis section nevertheless reports a per-domain agreement rate of 60.0%, so the withholding statement is stale or false.

"No screening log is recorded for this review" and the search yield cannot be shown. Later sections display a 21-record cascade, a 16-trial screening summary, and a registration-by-registration exclusion table. These surfaces disagree about whether screening records and counts exist.

The prominent question identifies studies only as "One trial," "the other three registrations," and "one of them." Those descriptors stand in for trial identities at the point where the page states its evidence inventory. The answering trial is CLEAR Outcomes, NCT02993406; the other registrations are not identified there.

The page asks, "what is the effect on each trial's own registered primary outcome?" The page does not answer that question: it presents neither trial-level outcome results nor effect estimates, despite both named registry records having results.

"2 trials, and no two share a registered primary outcome family." Both named trials register CDI recurrence as a primary outcome, expressed as the percentage of participants with recurrence. Their records also contain corresponding adverse-event primary-outcome families. The stated reason for declaring the trials outcome-incompatible is therefore contradicted by the displayed registry information.

"Registered endpoint definitions are recorded per trial on this object." No per-trial endpoint definitions, event counts, denominators, treatment/control values, or effect estimates are displayed. The contributing-trials table contains headers but no trial rows, so a reader cannot reconstruct either trial's result.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The canonical object and registration location are shown only as em dashes, the Sources table is empty, and the trial-level numerical inputs are absent. The reproducibility claim is false for the page as delivered.

"Risk-of-bias assessment grades trials contributing to a pooled result" and "No pooled estimate, risk-of-bias assessment or certainty rating is published for this question, because there is no combined result for them to describe." Risk of bias can be assessed for individual trials whether or not their results are pooled. Absence of a combined estimate does not justify the page's implication that trial-level risk-of-bias assessment is inapplicable.

“22 record(s) with eligibility undetermined” is given as a reason for the NOT READY status. The page later reports all 22 records as resolved into 7 excluded, 14 eligible and 1 not assessable, with an unscreened remainder of 0; the readiness message is stale or internally inconsistent.

“Pooled under random-effects with the REML random-effects, inverse-variance estimator on the log scale.” The fitted analysis is a mean-difference synthesis on the natural percentage-point scale, not the log scale.

The pooled result is “across 6 trials, against placebo,” and the precondition table says “all 6 readable trial(s) contribute one topic-vs-control randomised contrast.” The SPIRE-AI contribution is not a registered dose-matched contrast: the page pooled bococizumab 150 mg against the placebo intended for the 75 mg dose. Therefore the six-trial pool does not consistently implement the stated bococizumab-versus-placebo question.

SPIRE-SI contributes 71 treatment and 70 control participants, described as bococizumab 150 mg against placebo. The page acknowledges that SPIRE-SI has bococizumab, atorvastatin and placebo arms but does not identify which arm was omitted, so the displayed contrast and denominators cannot be independently reconstructed from the page.

“No single trial carries it” and the visual abstract says, “Leave-one-out: all 5 refits still exclude no difference; the estimate survives removal of any single trial.” A six-trial synthesis requires six leave-one-out refits, each with k=5. The displayed table contains only five omissions, omits SPIRE-FH, and labels every refit k=4, showing that it belongs to the earlier five-trial analysis.

The pooling-method section says, “This is a new analysis,” and presents REML, DL and PM sensitivity results as applying to the current answer. The table reports the earlier five-trial estimate near -55.46, not the current six-trial estimate -55.24. Its REML-HKSJ interval, -60.67 to -50.25, also conflicts with the page's quoted six-trial HKSJ output, -59.0796 to -51.4017.

The displayed analysis output states, “stored: MD -55.24 (-58.27 to -52.21) I^2 = 41.5”. Those are not the stored values shown elsewhere on the page. The page gives -55.24 (-57.92 to -52.56) and I-squared 56.8%, and separately admits that 41.5 was copied from another topic.

The visual abstract reports “6 trials, 4,252 participants.” The page supplies no calculation yielding 4,252. It elsewhere reports 4,449 registered participants, while the six displayed analysed-arm denominators sum to 3,969.

“Every row carries the value, the verbatim sentence it was read from, a resolvable link to the source, and whether the number was read or derived.” Five of the six pooled trials have no recorded source sentence, and their contributing-trial source cells contain only a colon. The numerical meta-analysis can be recalculated from the displayed estimates and intervals, but those five inputs cannot be traced to the claimed verbatim source evidence on the page.

The page-standard audit says two database queries were recorded with dates and counts and that the PRISMA arithmetic reconciles. The reader-facing search section says the ClinicalTrials.gov yield is not held, shows an empty results table, says PubMed was not executed, and says no screening log exists.

The page says, "Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page" and says it extracted per-trial arms, counts, analysed denominators and published effects. The Sources and Contributing trials tables contain no data rows, the canonical object and registration location are em dashes, and no per-arm denominators or effect estimates are displayed. The evidence numbers cannot be rebuilt from the page.

The page reports a fully reconciled cascade with 57 surfaced records, 47 role-located records and 2 eligible trials. It does not display the records or their dispositions: the remainder-screening and every-trial tables are empty, so readers cannot reproduce those counts or verify why candidates were excluded.

The summary says, "1 of 2 trial was confirmed: the drug is part of the randomised comparison. 1 trial was given in every arm, so it is background therapy rather than what the trial randomised." That adjudication conflicts with both displayed trials. The page expressly says FUTURE-3 randomised twice-daily versus three-times-daily bosentan and is in scope as an alternative dosing schedule; NCT01389856 compares bosentan with matching placebo. Neither supports the assertion that bosentan was merely non-randomised background therapy.

The analysis describes the comparator as "placebo or an inactive control" for its k=2 outcome. One of the two eligible trials, FUTURE-3, is a comparison of two bosentan dosing schedules, not placebo or inactive control.

The page says both trials have "NO walk-change and NO clinical-worsening outcome at any rank" and that neither registers a clinical-worsening outcome. NCT01389856 registers treatment failure as a primary outcome, together with time to weaning from inhaled nitric oxide and mechanical ventilation. The blanket assertion that neither trial has a clinical-worsening outcome does not match the displayed registry evidence.

The Summary of findings reports "Any shared clinical outcome | 2 | not pooled", and the Pooled result section says "Any shared clinical outcome. k = 2." The page repeatedly concludes that the trials share no estimand and that k pooled is zero. The k=2 entry is the number of eligible trials, not the number contributing to an actual shared clinical outcome; the displayed outcome is therefore stale or placeholder language.

The registration table says, "Certainty assessment | GRADE, recorded for 1 outcome(s) (GRADE)." Elsewhere the page says the purported outcome has no pooled estimate, any former rating is not shown, and no certainty rating is published. The GRADE status is internally inconsistent.

The GOSH section calls the analysis "Computable but uninformative at k = 2". A GOSH analysis is not computable from two merely eligible trials that have no shared estimand or displayed comparable effects. The page itself says no model was run and no between-study variance was estimated.

The page discusses individual trials using labels such as "EARLY", "COMPASS-2", "FUTURE-3", "1 of 2 trial" and "1 trial". EARLY and COMPASS-2 are not given registration identifiers at their mentions; Table 9 uses FUTURE-3 without NCT01223352; and the summary's anonymous "1 trial" adjudication does not identify which included trial it concerns.

The review concerns "adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension" and reports seven eligible trials. One included trial, NCT04039464, explicitly enrolled a pediatric pulmonary-hypertension population and therefore falls outside the stated adult population.

The randomized contrast is adding bosentan to established PAH-specific therapy versus continuing that background therapy alone. Several included trials do not test that contrast: NCT00120380 randomizes aerosolized iloprost versus placebo; NCT01100736 compares bosentan, sitaxsentan, placebo and endothelin-3 in a physiological study; NCT01352065 compares bosentan, ambrisentan and placebo; and NCT06317805 randomizes parenteral treprostinil plus double-oral therapy versus double-oral therapy.

"Seven trials are eligible" and "5 of 7 trials were confirmed: the drug is part of the randomised comparison." The page itself says two trials could not be verified from their arms and that "no other check has looked," yet it still presents all seven as eligible rather than unresolved.

"Extracted per trial on this object: registry id; design; arms; per-arm counts and the published effect; the randomised total, separately from the analysed denominator." The displayed contributing-trials table contains no trial rows. It supplies no arms, per-arm denominators, event counts, hazard ratio or interval, so the reported trial result cannot be rebuilt.

"Everything a third party needs to rebuild this page." The canonical-object location and registration fields are em dashes, the Sources table is empty, the ClinicalTrials.gov results table is empty, and no screening log or trial-level extraction is displayed.

Page-standard property P1 says "2 database queries recorded verbatim with dates and counts; PRISMA arithmetic reconciles" and P2 says the complete cascade is held. The reader receives one ClinicalTrials.gov query without its yield, a PubMed query marked not executed, no returned identifiers or dispositions, and empty screening tables. The cascade counts therefore cannot be independently reconstructed from the displayed search record.

"Time to first morbidity or mortality event. k = 7" and the summary-of-findings table assigns k=7 to that outcome. The page's own outcome audit says only four of seven trials register either a clinical-worsening or walk-change outcome, and only COMPASS-2 has posted results. Seven trials therefore do not contribute evidence to the displayed morbidity/mortality outcome.

The page alternately reports "Estimate withdrawn. k=1," "Time to first morbidity or mortality event. k = 7," "k_pooled | 1," and "k=7 and nothing was pooled." These statements conflate eligible, outcome-bearing, result-reporting and pooled trial counts. If nothing was pooled, k_pooled is zero rather than one; if only one result exists, the displayed outcome does not have seven contributing estimates.

The GOSH section says it is "Computable but uninformative at k = 7" with 127 subset estimates, and the meta-regression section discusses fitting a regression on seven points. The page displays no effects for seven trials and repeatedly says only one trial has posted results. A seven-study GOSH subset analysis or seven-point meta-regression is not computable from the evidence shown.

The page compares COMPASS-2 with a trial called "early" or "EARLY" when explaining why their registry arm structures are indistinguishable. The referenced EARLY trial is identified only by a descriptor in those passages; no registration identifier is supplied there or in the displayed seven-trial inventory.

The review asks, "In adults with WHO group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension, what is the effect of bosentan compared with placebo or no active pulmonary vasodilator on exercise capacity and on clinical worsening?" The page does not evaluate that clinical-effect question. It reports a registry-endpoint and poolability audit, has no pooled or per-trial clinical effects, lists zero source layers, and states that PubMed was not executed.

The headline and summary call these "four eligible trials" in adults with WHO group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension. The displayed material does not establish population eligibility and later expressly labels eligibility as not assessable because the sources are empty. NCT00377455 is described as a study in systemic-scleroderma patients with pulmonary hypertension, while NCT01827059 concerns exercise-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension in congenital heart disease; the page displays no eligibility details adjudicating either population against its stated scope.

"4 of 4 trials were confirmed: the drug is part of the randomised comparison." The page's own precondition assessment says all four trials lack readable arm roles and that contribution of a randomized contrast cannot be assessed. Merely listing bosentan among a registry record's interventions does not establish its randomized arm role.

"Extracted per trial on this object: registry id; design; arms; per-arm counts and the published effect; the randomised total, separately from the analysed denominator."
